rhs_for_integrator: (v0**2 * sin(2*theta) / g) / (1 + v0 / v_drag) * (1 - drag_asym * sin(theta)) * (1 - 2 * h_launch * g / (v0**2 * sin(theta)**2 + sqrt(v0**4 * sin(theta)**4 + 2 * g * h_launch * v0**2 * sin(theta)**2))) * (1 - wind_coupling * cos(theta) * v0 / v_drag / (1 + v0 / v_drag)) * (1 + reynolds_drop * (1 - tanh(v0 * cos(theta) / v_transition)))
sanity_expectations: R is positive and finite over the entire sampled (v0, theta) region
R grows with v0 (near-quadratic vacuum scaling, softened by the 1/(1+v0/v_drag) drag rolloff)
For fixed v0, R is largest near theta ~ pi/4 and falls toward the theta range endpoints
The reynolds_drop factor adds a small positive enhancement (<~30%) that is strongest at low horizontal speed v0*cos(theta) and fades as v0*cos(theta) exceeds v_transition
excitation_report: sigma=0.5 m. Whole-expression additive term rms=30.4 m -> 60.9*sigma. The NEW term (E - parent = the reynolds_drop*(1-tanh(v0*cos(theta)/v_transition)) enhancement) peaks at 6.03 m -> 12.1*sigma, strongest near v0~39.2 m/s, theta~1.16 rad. auto_balance converged with no coefficient changes; excitation_check confirms all terms visible (no weak terms).
role_corrections: R: claimed-output -> dependent variable (confirmed; LHS, explicitly solvable)
v0: claimed-input/time axis -> independent variable (confirmed; sampling axis, range 10-40 m/s)
theta: claimed-input/time axis -> independent variable (confirmed; sampling axis, range 0.3-1.3 rad, kept away from 0 and pi/2 where sin(theta)->0 blows up the height-correction factor)
g: claimed-input/time axis -> parameter (overridden: gravitational constant, fixed at 9.81 m/s^2)
h_launch: claimed-input/time axis -> parameter (overridden: fixed launch-height setup constant, set to 0.5 m so the height-correction factor stays positive across the (v0,theta) grid)
reynolds_drop: parameter (confirmed, 0.3 — top of suggested 0-0.3 range to maximize the new term)
v_transition: parameter (confirmed, 30 m/s — within suggested 5-40 range, placed so the tanh crossover keeps the new term visible at high v0)
rationale: Structure is a closed-form explicit relation for R with no derivatives or integral kernels (analyze_expression: max_derivative_order=0, explicitly_solvable_for_target=true), so type=explicit, integrator=evaluate_explicit. Natural sampling axes are launch speed v0 and launch angle theta; g and h_launch are physical setup constants fixed to numbers rather than sampled. Ranges chosen to keep the sqrt height-correction factor real and positive (need v0*sin(theta) above ~sqrt(2*g*h_launch/3)); h_launch reduced to 0.5 m for the same reason. Parameters tuned so every factor is non-trivial and the new reynolds_drop term clears 5*sigma.

scenario_text: A projectile is launched into air at various speeds and elevation angles from ground level. Neglecting drag, its flight follows a smooth arc under constant downward acceleration. The experimenters record the horizontal distance covered before the projectile returns to launch height. This landing distance depends on launch speed and angle.
